items.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears

1.text: Tech stocks around the world went down. Investors are worried about the AI industry. They fear that AI growth is slowing down. The US midterms are also making investors nervous. People think the government might look more closely at how companies build data centres. They also think there could be tougher rules for the AI industry. Because of these fears, many people sold their shares in tech companies. Investors are watching the US midterms carefully now. They want to see what will happen to data centres and AI companies in the future.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the story?
opts: Investors are buying more AI shares than ever.
Data centres are closing all over the world.
Tech stocks dropped due to fears about AI and US midterms.
The US midterms were cancelled by tech companies.

quiz.q: What does the word 'plunge' mean in the headline?
What might receive tougher scrutiny from the government?
True or False: Investors are worried about possible tougher rules for the AI industry.

2.text: Global tech stocks have dropped sharply as investors worry about a slowdown in the artificial intelligence industry. The upcoming US midterms are adding to these concerns. Investors react to the possibility of tougher scrutiny regarding the construction of new data centres, which are essential for AI technology. Furthermore, there are growing fears that the government may introduce stricter regulations for the entire AI sector. Because of these combined factors, confidence in technology companies has fallen, leading to widespread selling in global markets. Investors remain cautious as they monitor how political changes in the United States might impact the future growth and regulation of AI businesses and their infrastructure.

quiz.q: What is the main cause of the drop in global tech stocks?
opts: Fears of an AI slowdown and US midterm concerns
The closing of all tech businesses in the US
A sudden rise in the price of data centres
A lack of electricity for data centres

quiz.q: In the text, what does the word 'scrutiny' mean?
What kind of construction might face tougher scrutiny?
True or False: The text states that investors are unconcerned about the US midterms.

3.text: Global technology stocks have experienced a sharp decline as investors grapple with heightened fears of a slowdown in the artificial intelligence sector. Adding to the market instability are the upcoming US midterm elections, which have raised concerns over future policy directions. Investors have reacted strongly to the possibility of tougher government scrutiny surrounding the construction of data centres, which are critical to supporting AI workloads. Additionally, there is anxiety over potential increases in regulation targeting the broader AI industry. These combined worries have prompted a wave of selling across international markets, reflecting diminished confidence among shareholders. As the US midterms approach, financial markets are keeping a close watch on political developments that could lead to stricter oversight, potentially impacting the expansion plans and valuation of major technology firms involved in AI infrastructure.

quiz.q: Which statement best summarizes the main focus of the article?
opts: Data centre construction has been banned across the United States.
Investors are ignoring political events to focus entirely on AI technology.
Tech stocks fell as US midterms heightened fears over AI growth and regulation.
The AI industry has stopped all future building projects worldwide.

quiz.q: What does the word 'heightened' mean as used in the text?
What specific infrastructure is mentioned as facing potential tougher scrutiny?

opts: The text says this is impossible

items.title: Trump signs order on Oval Office decor

1.text: Donald Trump signed a new order. This order stops future presidents from changing the Oval Office. The Oval Office is a famous room in the White House. Trump made this decision after he made many big changes to the room's decor. He also tore down the White House East Wing. Now, future leaders cannot change the Oval Office decor like he did. Trump wants the room to stay the way it is now.

opts: Trump signed an order to stop future presidents from changing the Oval Office.
Trump built a new East Wing for the White House.
Future presidents will change the Oval Office every year.

opts: The decoration and style of a room

quiz.q: What part of the White House did Trump tear down?
Which statement is TRUE according to the story?

2.text: Donald Trump has signed a new executive order regarding the White House. This order prevents future presidents from changing the decor of the Oval Office. The decision was made after Trump introduced a series of major changes to the famous room's interior design. Along with altering the Oval Office decor, Trump also tore down the East Wing of the White House. Because of his new order, future leaders will not have the power to undo his changes or redecorate the Oval Office according to their own tastes. The order ensures that the current look of the Oval Office remains protected from any future modifications by coming presidents.

What did Trump do to the White House decor before signing the order?
opts: He allowed future presidents to choose the design.

quiz.q: Which statement is TRUE based on the text?
opts: The order was signed by a future president.
Trump tore down the East Wing of the White House.
Future presidents can easily change the Oval Office.
Trump preserved the East Wing without any changes.

3.text: Donald Trump has signed an official order designed to block future presidents from altering the decor of the Oval Office. This action comes directly after Trump completed a series of substantial modifications to the iconic room's interior aesthetic. In addition to these major changes inside the Oval Office, Trump also tore down the White House East Wing. By signing this order, Trump aims to protect the current state of the room, ensuring that subsequent commanders-in-chief cannot redecorate or reverse the design choices he has implemented. The order effectively freezes the Oval Office decor, preventing future administrations from putting their own personal stamp on the famous workspace.

quiz.q: What main action did Trump take according to the report?

items.title: White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses

1.text: US media reports say some people want to replace Pete Hegseth. He may also face an impeachment vote. At the same time, rumors say Mark Rubio wants to run for president. These reports came after Republicans lost elections. However, the White House denies that Pete Hegseth and Mark Rubio will leave their jobs. The White House says both men are staying in their positions. They will continue their work despite the rumors and the election results.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the story?
opts: Pete Hegseth won a major election.
Mark Rubio was voted out of office.
The White House denies Hegseth and Rubio are leaving their jobs.
The US media elected a new president.

quiz.q: What does the word 'denies' mean in the text?
What might Pete Hegseth face according to reports?
True or False: Mark Rubio is rumored to be looking at a presidential run.
opts: The text says he already won

2.text: Following recent Republican election losses, US media reports claim there are growing calls to replace Pete Hegseth. Reports also state that Hegseth could face a possible impeachment vote. Meanwhile, other rumors suggest that Mark Rubio is eyeing a future presidential run. Despite these media claims, the White House has officially denied that either man will be leaving his position. Officials state that Hegseth and Rubio will remain in their current roles. The White House pushback comes as commentators discuss the fallout from the recent election results and speculate about potential changes in government leadership.

quiz.q: What is the main focus of the article?
opts: The results of a recent presidential vote
Mark Rubio starting his campaign for president
Pete Hegseth resigning from his position
The White House denying that Hegseth and Rubio are leaving

quiz.q: In the text, what does the word 'eyeing' mean?
What political event happened before these reports emerged?
opts: The White House hired new staff.

quiz.q: Which statement is TRUE according to the text?
opts: Pete Hegseth faces a potential impeachment vote according to media reports.
Mark Rubio has officially left his job.
The White House confirmed Hegseth will be replaced.

3.text: The White House has firmly rejected claims that Pete Hegseth and Mark Rubio will be stepping down from their positions in the wake of recent Republican election losses. US media reports had previously indicated that there were mounting calls to replace Hegseth, who is additionally facing the prospect of a potential impeachment vote. Simultaneously, separate reports surfaced speculating that Rubio is eyeing a potential presidential run. Despite these widespread media reports and political rumors, White House representatives insist that both officials will remain in their posts, dismissing speculation about impending staff departures following the unfavorable election outcomes.

quiz.q: What main message is the White House conveying?
opts: Reports about Hegseth and Rubio leaving their jobs are untrue.
An impeachment vote against Hegseth has passed.
The recent election results were a success for Republicans.
Hegseth and Rubio are retiring immediately.

quiz.q: What does 'surfaced' mean in this context?

items.title: Vance Criticizes Republican Defeat and Points to Iran War

1.text: Vice President Vance gave a very blunt assessment of a recent Republican election defeat. His strong critique was one of the sharpest breaks with a sitting president in recent memory. Vance blamed the election loss on a war with Iran. He spoke directly about why the Republicans lost. This event showed a big difference in opinion between the vice president and the sitting president. People were surprised by his honest words about the political situation and the war.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the story?
opts: Vance strongly criticized a Republican election loss and blamed a war.
The president ended the war with Iran.

quiz.q: What does the word 'blunt' mean in the text?
What did Vance blame for the election defeat?
True or False: Vance's actions showed a sharp break with a sitting president.

2.text: Vice President Vance recently shared a blunt assessment regarding a Republican election defeat. His scathing critique marked one of the sharpest breaks with a sitting president in recent memory. During his comments, Vance directly blamed a war with Iran for the political loss. By speaking out so strongly, Vance highlighted a major rift between himself and the current president. It is rare for a sitting vice president to criticize political outcomes and presidential context so openly. This sudden public split has drawn significant attention because it shows deep disagreement at the highest level of government over the impact of foreign conflict on domestic elections.

3.text: In a remarkable political development, Vice President Vance delivered a blunt assessment of a recent Republican election defeat, attributing the loss to an ongoing war with Iran. His scathing critique represents one of the sharpest public breaks with a sitting president in recent memory. By explicitly linking the electoral setback to the foreign conflict, Vance created a visible divide between his perspective and that of the current administration. Such an open disagreement from a serving vice president is exceptionally rare, shedding light on internal tensions regarding the political fallout of international military actions. Observers noted that Vance did not hold back in his evaluation, marking a memorable moment of public discord within top political ranks.

items.title: What Democrats can and can't do with their new power after taking Congress

1.text: Democrats have new power in Congress. They can vote and pass new legislation. This means they can make new rules and laws. However, Donald Trump is still the president. Trump has veto power. Veto means he can stop a law from passing even if Congress votes for it. So, Democrats can approve new laws in Congress, but they cannot make every law happen alone. They must remember that President Trump can still block their plans with his veto.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the story?
opts: Congress cannot vote on any new legislation.
Democrats have new power, but Trump can still veto their laws.
Trump lost all of his power to the Democrats.
Democrats and Trump agree on every new law.

quiz.q: What does the word 'veto' mean in the text?
opts: To stop a law from passing
To vote for a new leader

quiz.q: What can Democrats do with their new power?
opts: They can stop Trump from using his veto.
They can remove the president immediately.
They can change the president's name.

quiz.q: Which statement is true based on the text?
opts: Democrats can make every law happen alone.
Congress is not allowed to vote.
Trump no longer has veto power.

2.text: After taking Congress, Democrats now hold significant new power in government. With this position, they have the ability to vote legislation through and advance their policy goals. This allows them to pass new laws in the legislative branch. However, their power is not unlimited because Donald Trump remains president. President Trump still holds veto power over any bills that Congress passes. A presidential veto can prevent proposed legislation from officially becoming law. Therefore, while Democrats can successfully vote on and pass legislation through Congress, they must still deal with the fact that President Trump can block their bills. They cannot enact laws completely on their own without facing the president's potential veto.

quiz.q: What is the main topic of the text?
opts: Why Donald Trump lost his veto power
How to vote in American elections
The limits and abilities of the Democrats' new power

quiz.q: What does 'legislation' mean in the text?
Who still holds veto power?
Which statement is true according to the text?
opts: Donald Trump cannot stop bills passed by Congress.
Democrats can pass laws completely on their own without limits.
Democrats can vote legislation through Congress.
Trump has lost his role as president.

3.text: Following their recent takeover of Congress, Democrats have gained substantial new authority within the legislative process. Equipped with this political power, Democrats now possess the capability to vote legislation through the chamber. This milestone enables them to shape the legislative agenda and push forward proposed bills. Nevertheless, there are distinct boundaries to what they can achieve. Donald Trump remains in the presidency and retains his full veto power. This constitutional mechanism allows President Trump to reject and block any legislation passed by Congress, preventing it from taking effect as law. Consequently, despite their ability to approve bills in Congress, Democrats cannot enact legislation entirely at will, as the threat of a presidential veto continues to stand in their path.

quiz.q: What is the main focus of this article?
opts: The balance between Democratic congressional power and Trump's veto authority
Why President Trump decided to give up his power
The process of electing a new president in Congress
A complete list of laws recently passed by Democrats

quiz.q: In the context of the text, what does 'retains' mean?
What specific action can Democrats take after taking Congress?
opts: They can eliminate the presidential veto.
They can pass laws without any opposition.

quiz.q: Which of the following statements is FALSE based on the text?
opts: Democrats can pass laws without facing any presidential veto.
Trump still has the power to veto legislation.
Trump can block legislation passed by Congress.
Democrats gained new power after taking Congress.

items.title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation

1.text: Five trade unions in France joined together for a national day of action. Workers started strikes and protests across the country. They want to show their power and make their voices heard. Many people are participating in these events. The unions promised a big national mobilisation. Because of this, many services in France may stop or work slowly. The unions hope that this action will bring changes for the workers. More protests are expected to happen as the unions continue to work together on this big day.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the story?
opts: Five French unions organised a national day of strikes and protests.
French unions decided to stop all protests forever.
Only one small union is striking in France today.

quiz.q: What does 'mobilisation' mean in this text?
How many trade unions joined the national day of action?

2.text: Five of France's trade unions have joined a widespread wave of strikes and protests as part of a national day of action. The unions have promised a strong national mobilisation to push for their demands. This coordinated effort means that workers from different sectors across the country are walking out of their jobs and taking to the streets. Public transport, schools, and other services could face severe disruptions throughout the day. Union leaders hope this large-scale action will demonstrate their strength and force officials to listen to their concerns. The national mobilisation marks a significant moment of unity among the five different labor organisations as they push forward together.

3.text: Five of France's leading trade unions have joined forces in a widespread wave of strikes and protests, marking a powerful national day of action. Promising a full-scale national mobilisation, the labor organisations have called upon workers nationwide to demonstrate their collective strength. The coordinated strike action is expected to cause notable disruptions to public services, transport networks, and various business sectors throughout the country. By uniting five major unions under a single cause, labor leaders aim to send a strong message to both employers and government officials. As citizens gear up for the widespread movement, public attention remains focused on the scale of the participation and the potential impact of this massive display of union solidarity across France.
